claims.claim: The standard full-length 35 mm roll has always been 36 exposures.
claims.episode_span: A typical 35-millimeter roll held thirty-six exposures; after exposure the film had to be developed in a darkroom or sent to a lab
claims.supporting_quote: The standard full-length roll has always been 36 exposures (assuming a standard 24×36 frame size).

claims.claim: Photographic film is a base coated with a gelatin emulsion containing microscopic light-sensitive silver halide crystals.
claims.episode_span: each new image still required fresh silver halide crystals suspended in gelatin, fresh baths of developer and fixer
claims.supporting_quote: Photographic film is a strip or sheet of transparent film base coated on one side with a gelatin emulsion containing microscopically small light-sensitive silver halide crystals, for the purpose of taking photographs

claims.claim: The charge-coupled device was invented in 1969 by Willard Boyle and George E. Smith, who were researching MOS technology at Bell Labs.
claims.episode_span: Engineers at laboratories including Bell Labs and later at companies such as Kodak and Sony began with the question of what physics actually demands to register light
claims.supporting_quote: In the late 1960s, Willard Boyle and George E. Smith at Bell Labs were researching MOS technology while working on semiconductor bubble memory . They realized that an electric charge was the analog of the magnetic bubble and that it could be stored on a tiny MOS capacitor. As it was fairly straightforward to fabricate a series of MOS capacitors in a row, they connected a suitable voltage to them so that the charge could be stepped along from one to the next. [ 3 ] This led to the invention of the charge-coupled device by Boyle and Smith in 1969.

claims.claim: The Bayer color filter array (half green, one quarter red, one quarter blue), named for its inventor Bryce Bayer of Eastman Kodak, lets a single sensor capture color information.
claims.episode_span: A third step introduced the Bayer color filter array over the silicon photosites, allowing a single sensor to capture red, green, and blue information without multiple exposures or separate film layers
claims.supporting_quote: The filter pattern is half green, one quarter red and one quarter blue, hence is also called BGGR , RGBG , [ 1 ] [ 2 ] GRBG , [ 3 ] or RGGB . [ 4 ] It is named after its inventor, Bryce Bayer of Eastman Kodak .

claims.claim: Polaroid Corporation pioneered instant cameras, which use self-developing film to produce a print shortly after the picture is taken.
claims.episode_span: when instant cameras like those from Polaroid shortened the wait between exposure and print
claims.supporting_quote: An instant camera is a camera which uses self-developing film to create a chemically developed print shortly after taking the picture. Polaroid Corporation pioneered (and patented ) consumer-friendly instant cameras and film

claims.claim: Photographic printing paper carries a light-sensitive emulsion whose most common chemistry is gelatin silver.
claims.episode_span: then printed on light-sensitive paper that itself contained silver compounds
claims.supporting_quote: The light-sensitive layer of the paper is called the emulsion , and functions similarly to photographic film . The most common chemistry used is gelatin silver , but other alternatives have also been used.
